title: Authentication: cookie session, JWT, OAuth and OpenID

videos.script:
A web server has no memory. {{http}} Every request arrives on its own, and if the server wants to know who sent it, it has to be told, every time.

There are three ways to tell it. {{three}} A session cookie, where the server remembers and the browser carries a meaningless id. A signed token, where the meaning travels inside. And somebody else checking the password for you, which is OAuth.

Today the planner gets a small server of its own, with one account. {{curl}} You sign in with curl, and watch the cookie arrive.

Then a JWT, written by hand. {{jwt}} You will see that anybody can read it, and that nobody can change it.

Then the flow a browser app uses with a provider. {{oauth}} The authorization code, with PKCE. You check it against the standard's own numbers, and the numbers agree.
